correctness.rationale: Every clique-core independent set contains zero or one core vertex. Summing pendant choices conditional on this yields W=prod_i A_i+sum_i u_i prod_(r≠i) A_r, with A_i=0 or q=2^b. Cases z≥2, z=1, z=0 give respectively 0, ±q^(h-1), q^(h-1)(q+h-2j). For even h and q≤h the last vanishes exactly on the Hamming shell j*=(h+q)/2, giving rank and sharp spectral gap. Fourier inversion of the support of at-most-one-bad leaf blocks gives the kernel δ_(ycore,0)q^-h(1-h+qz); subtract the Krawtchouk j* core-shell kernel exactly if resonant. Summing absolute kernel entries proves the displayed endpoint norms, with the simplified no-resonance negative mass (h-1)(1-1/q)^h. Translation-averaging any range projection proves the Fourier convolution projection minimizes ℓ1 and ℓ∞ norms. The rank fraction and fixed-h limit follow from the formulas.

value.rationale: A clique-core corona with private leaf bundles is a natural two-parameter graph family. Its exact signed Fourier spectrum, resonance shell and optimal endpoint range-projection norms distinguish spectral invertibility/rank from endpoint amplification, with a sharp limit 2h-1 even when the rank fraction tends to zero. These are reusable graph-harmonic invariants and natural infinite-family classification, not a single finite count.

limitations: Uniform b per core vertex and clique cores only; heterogenous bundles excluded.
Resonant endpoint norm is a finite explicit Krawtchouk sum rather than closed elementary formula.
Fourier optimal range projection does not imply an arbitrary norm-minimizing inverse outside the claimed problem.
